svg.data-fans: 3x hot-swappable 2+1 redundant, exhaust airflow; system front-to-back
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO, ITU-T SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 (G.8265.1 default, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 with additional licence; T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC), Class C accuracy
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS SMA in, 1PPS SMB in/out, 10MHz SMB in/out, ToD RJ45 in/out
svg.data-gnss: internal receiver for master clock implementations, enabling a T-GM source at the cell site without additional equipment
svg.data-timing-cables: 50 ohm SMA coax with 1/4-36UNS-2B for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coax with 10-32UNF-2A for 1PPS and 10MHz; shielded RJ45 for ToD
svg.data-nos: NOS integration is necessary to activate the timing features
svg.data-optics-sfp: 1G SFP SX, LX, EX, ZX (datasheet compatible transceiver types)
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: 10G SFP+ SR, LR, ER, ZR (datasheet compatible transceiver types)
svg.data-bmc-role: individual BMC for automatic and remote platform health monitoring

The HIG's Figure 5 overview callout, pointing at the same eight cages, instead reads '8 x 2.5G SFP'. Same ports, same measure, different value. The manifest carries 1G because two independent statements - one in each document, one of them a table rather than a drawing callout - agree on it against a single callout label.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["sfp-1g"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide or NOS port-capability note for ports 4-11","what":"sfp-port-speed"},{"note":"HIG section 8 says the designated grounding location 'is located on the side of the router' and shows both locations in Figure 22, but never says which side, and the figure is an unlabelled flank elevation. They are drawn on the RIGHT flank because the front faceplate prints its earth symbol at the right-hand end, which is a reason and not a source. Their positions along the depth ARE measured (Figure 22, anchored on the 302 mm chassis bar).","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ground-1","ground-2","ground-3","ground-4"],"wanted":"a photograph of the real unit's flanks, or a figure captioned with the side","what":"grounding-flank"},{"note":"The rear face carries two plain plates either side of the fan modules, measured at x 18.1-69.6 and 229.3-280.0 and drawn at 18.6 and 229.3 after the matched-scale comparison. Each is 51.5 mm wide - one fan module - and each lands on the 52.3 mm fan pitch continued outwards, so the rear reads as five fan positions of which three are populated. The vendor says 3 fans and 2+1 redundancy and names no blanking part, so these are drawn as decor rather than as bays with fillers: a bay with no orderable occupant would be a promise the parts list does not make. If they are in fact fan-bay blanks this should become two more bays and a filler component.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"a photograph of the rear with a plate removed, or a UfiSpace accessory list naming a fan blank","what":"rear-blank-plates"},{"note":"'FAN <0' / 'FAN <1' / 'FAN <2' appear at the top of each fan module's right-hand strip in the HIG rear elevation. If they are chassis printing they are hidden behind the modules; if module printing, the shared ufispace/fan-402825 component cannot carry a per-position digit. Neither is drawn. Recorded here for the same reason, and in the same words, as ufispace/s6301-56stp - a photograph of an empty fan bay would settle which metal carries the ink.","reason":"needs-hardware","scope":["fans"],"wanted":"photograph of an empty S9501-18SMT fan bay","what":"fan-position-legends"},{"note":"HIG section 10 tables the five system lamps (GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR), the PSU FRU lamp, the Fan FRU lamp and the management jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The eight corner dots on the RJ45 block and the fourteen up/down arrows in the SFP and SFP+ lands therefore keep their component default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nine rows elsewhere in those same tables read 'need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than simply undocumented; that is a different fix, and the reason this is filed as vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rj45-1g","sfp-1g","sfp-plus","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"A two-high ganged SFP block normally mirrors, so that both rows' bail latches stay reachable, and std/sfp-ganged draws an asymmetric aperture (module slot above, cage lip below) that shows the difference. The only elevation that resolves these cages is HIG Figure 9, and Figure 9 prints its large annotation numerals ON the cages, covering exactly the detail that would settle it. The rows are drawn belly-to-belly, the lower row rotate: 180, because that is the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S3: upper rotate 0 over lower 180, both bails outward) and the port lamps between the rows point up over down - the rule and the lamps, not an observation of the metal.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["sfp-1g","sfp-plus"],"wanted":"a straight-on high-resolution front photograph, or a vendor 3D model","what":"sfp-row-mirroring"},{"note":"ufispace/fan-402825 states no draw and its own contract records the search across all 573 converted documents: eight UfiSpace datasheets name the part only as an ordering line, with no wattage anywhere near it. This HIG is the same - it weighs the fan FRU at 90 g and tables its lamp, and its only wattage figures are the system's 85 W maximum and the 200 W per-circuit reserve, neither of which is a fan's draw. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis total is a floor.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ufispace/fan-402825@1"],"wanted":"a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet","what":"fru-power-unpublished"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"2+1","redundancy-note":"2+1 - hot swappable fan modules with 2+1 redundancy support (UfiSpace datasheet, staged intake)"},"description":"vendor numbers the modules FAN 0, FAN 1, FAN 2 on the rear face","index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster - the out-of-band RJ45, a USB Type-A service port, the RS-232 console on RJ45 and the recessed reset button. Four media, one job, and the vendor draws them as one cluster; this device carries no BITS jack, unlike its S9510 and M3000 siblings","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9501-18SMT","name":"s9501-18smt","portfolio":{"family":"Disaggregated Cell Site Gateway Router","line":"Telecoms","series":"S9500 Series"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"attrs":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet (Specifications / Accessories / Environmental / Performance / Regulatory Compliance) and HIG (the Port Overview table for reach and speed, section 11 for the console settings). Compliance transcribed as printed and not tidied."},"bottom":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"estimated - no source in the intake shows the underside. The compliance sticker is the house convention (every shipped unit carries one) at an estimated position. A bottom view mirrors LEFT and RIGHT; the sticker is the only content and it is the only thing on the face, so the axis was checked and does not bite."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet '1 RU, 440 x 302 x 43.5mm', 'Weight: 4.34 kg (without FRU)', repeated verbatim by the HIG Component Physical Information table ('S9501-18SMT (W x D x H) 440 x 302 x 43.5mm', 'Chassis without FRU 9.57lb (4.34kg)'). 440 IS THE BODY, NOT THE RACK FACE: the HIG Space Clearance section says 'The S9501-18SMT width is 17.32 inches (44cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', and the accessory list orders the brackets separately (50.4 x 43 x 20 mm each, 2 pcs). The brackets are not drawn. Depth 302 is 'without the field replaceable units'; HIG Fig 5 also dimensions 327.4 mm over the PSU handles, and Space Clearance states the PSU handle stands 27 mm proud and the fan handle 25 mm - 302 + 27 = 329, which is the same fact to within the drawing."},"fan-component":{"note":"reuses ufispace/fan-402825@1. This device orders FAN-402818-HC where the S9510-28DC orders FAN-402825-HD, and the two are different part numbers - but the HIG's Component Physical Information table gives this fan the same 51.5 x 57.8 x 42.2 mm envelope as that one, and the Figure 8 elevation draws the same face: red tube handle on the left, hex rotor grille, a red E exhaust badge, a knurled captive thumbscrew and a status lamp. The per-device part number is carried in the configurations' component-attrs, which is where a FRU model belongs. ONE DIFFERENCE WAS SEEN AND NOT MODELLED: this figure draws the status lamp low on the module's right strip, below the thumbscrew, where ufispace/fan-402825 draws it top-left."},"front-figure-scale":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - HIG page 12, the Figure 9 port-overview elevation. GATE 1: the drawn faceplate measures 3936 x 393 px (x 737-4673, y 4147-4540 on the 600 dpi page), which is 8.945 px/mm against 440 mm and 9.034 px/mm against 43.5 mm - 1.0% apart, so the figure is orthographic and carries geometry. The band ABOVE y 4147 is the chassis top surface seen in slight perspective, not part of the 43.5 face; including it gives 9.52 px/mm and a 6% error, which is how this figure reads as schematic if the chamfer is measured as metal. Every front coordinate below is measured at 8.945/9.034 px/mm unless it says otherwise."},"ground-mark":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - the earth symbol in a circle printed at (433.1, 22.0), about 4 mm across, at the far right of the faceplate. No connector is there: the bonding points are on a flank (HIG section 8), and this mark is taken as pointing at them. Drawn with common/ground-symbol at its own 6.0 contract size."},"lane-lamps":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - every SFP and SFP+ column carries one up arrow and one down arrow in the land between its two rows, up serving the top port and down the bottom. Arrow centres measured at 5.4 and 9.1 mm from the cage's left edge on the SFP block and 5.5 and 9.4 on the SFP+ blocks; drawn at 5.4 and 9.1 on both, which is within the spread of the eight measurements and keeps two 3.6 mm common/led-arrow parts from overlapping. Vertical centre 22.0 on both blocks."},"led-semantics":{"note":"HIG section 10, pages 20-21, transcribed rather than only cited. Each front-panel lamp carries its own vocabulary and several rows are annotated 'need NOS to activate this feature'. STAT is the one that differs from the S9510-28DC family: it has a Solid Yellow row here, 'System boot complete (DIAG OS)', which the S9510's table does not carry. The PSU FRU and Fan FRU tables belong to the modules and are transcribed in ufispace/psu-201-dc, psu-201-ac and fan-402825. The management jack is declared per element because its left lamp is green for 1G and its right amber for 10M/100M."},"left":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-fraction - HIG Figure 22 shows a flank as a plain bar carrying two rows of small holes and the rack-bracket fixings; the angle render shows the same on the left flank. AXIS: x = 0 is the REAR on a left view (viewer3d.js convention). The hole rows are drawn as decor at an estimated pitch; the three screw heads are estimated. Content is honestly sparse rather than blank - this face is plain metal."},"lifecycle":{"note":"searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9501-18SMT end of life end of sale' - no announcement found; the product page is live, the unit is listed by resellers and it carries an Open Compute Project product entry. none-announced is a real finding, not an omission."},"mgmt-oob-usb":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - one silver bezel x 165.2-182.0, y 13.9-35.1, holding the out-of-band RJ45 above a USB-A socket. THE BEZEL HEIGHT IS THE ARITHMETIC: 21.2 mm is std/rj45-ganged (11.0) plus std/usb-a (4.5) plus the 5.7 mm white land drawn between them, which is why the jack is the ganged part and not the 16 x 14 std/rj45. Jack aperture measured 12.6 wide against the ganged contract's 12.7. ORIENTATION READ AT 6x ZOOM: the OOB jack is keyway-UP (rotate 180) with its green and amber lamps in the TOP corners, measured at (166.9-169.6, 14.8-16.8) and (178.1-180.3, 15.1-16.7). A network icon is printed above the bezel at (171.9-175.4, 9.3-11.8) and the USB trident below at (171.2-175.4, 36.4-38.6); both are drawn as path marks. The silver bezel is PANEL, drawn as decor - without it a dark jack on a dark faceplate is invisible. THE ART MISMATCH THIS ENTRY USED TO RECORD IS FIXED: std/usb-a@1 drew a blue USB-3 tongue where the datasheet says '1 x USB 2.0 Type-A port', and it was left alone because the colour belongs to the shared part rather than to this device. The shared part now carries a `usb2` skin and the placement asks for it. One shade of difference remains and is not worth another skin: USB-IF's colour for 2.0 is white and the vendor's drawing shows a black tongue."},"part-numbers":{"note":"none stated. Neither the datasheet nor the HIG prints an orderable chassis SKU; the datasheet's 'Available to Order' section names only the PSUs (PSU-201-DISB, PSU-201-AISB) and the fan (FAN-402818-HC). No SKU is invented, so the configurations carry none - the same finding, and the same treatment, as m3000-14xc."},"power":{"note":"two figures, two measures, no conflict. Datasheet Environmental: 'Typical power: 52 Watts (no transceiver)' - a typical, explicitly with the cages empty. HIG Connecting Power, stated identically in the DC and AC sections: 'The maximum system power consumption is 85 watts' - a maximum, with NO configuration or ambient named. Both are carried. power-envelope is 'unstated' rather than 'bare' because only the 52 W figure declares its scope and the field describes the entry as a whole; saying 'bare' would silently extend the datasheet's qualifier to the HIG's number. PSU inputs from the datasheet (AC 100-240 V 3 A, DC -36 to -75 V 8 A); per-PSU rating lives on the ufispace/psu-201-* contracts, not here. The HIG's 'a reserve of at least 200 watts on each power circuit' is a provisioning instruction and is not recorded as a draw."},"psu-bays":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured with a stated residual. The PSU LAMPS are the only unambiguous feature on both modules: their centres sit at x 51.5 and 110.1, a pitch of 58.63. The bay seams read 58.69 and the blue latches 59.24, so the pitch is taken as 58.7. The absolute left edge is softer: the lamp (via ufispace/psu-201-dc's own art) puts the module at x 5.68, the seam at 6.5, and the divider legend's centre line at 60.7 (which with a 58.7 - 50.5 = 8.2 mm divider puts them at 6.1 and 64.8). SETTLED BY RENDERING IT AND LOOKING: at 5.5 and 64.2 our two hard features land on the drawing's - the blue latch's right edge at 9.7 against a measured 9.73, and the two lamp centres at 51.3 and 110.0 against measured 51.48 and 110.11. The first draft's 5.9 put both 0.4 mm to the right of the figure. Bay size 50.5 x 40.2 is the HIG table, not measured. y = 1.7 is the family value (s9510-28dc uses 1.6 on the same 43.5 chassis) and matches the drawn module face (top edge 1.9-2.1, bottom 42.5-43.2) as well as this figure resolves. THE RENDER'S PSU ART IS NOT OUR COMPONENT'S ART - the drawn lamp sits 3 mm further from the module's right edge than ufispace/psu-201-dc draws it, which is why the lamp cannot be used as an absolute anchor and only as a pitch ruler."},"psu-divider":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - a dark strip between the two bays, x 56.0-64.2, carrying PSU0 printed downward, a pointer pair, and PSU1, all rotated 90 degrees. Legend spans read off HIG page 12 at 27 px/mm: PSU0 y 4.4-17.0, the triangles 18.7-25.9, PSU1 27.6-38.8. The strip is decor (it is chassis metal); the legends are silkscreen. Vendor spells the bays PSU0 and PSU1, so the psus group is index-origin 0. THE POINTER PAIR IS DRAWN AS TWO PATH MARKS, NOT AS THE CHARACTERS - the arrowhead glyphs come out as empty boxes in every rasteriser without a symbol font, which is visible in the render and invisible to lint."},"rear":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured from the Figure 8 elevation. Three fan modules with their faces at x 71.8, 124.1 and 176.4 - a 52.3 mm pitch taken from the red exhaust badges (52.39, 52.39) and the green lamps (52.28, 52.16), against a 51.5 mm module, so the gap between modules is 0.8. Bay y 0.7, size 51.5 x 42.2 from the HIG table. TWO BLANK PLATES flank them, x 18.1-69.6 and 229.3-280.0, each 51.5 wide and each landing exactly on the fan pitch continued outwards (19.5 and 228.7). They are drawn as decor and their identity is a gap - see rear-blank-plates. Hex vent field x 282.5-432.5, y 4.2-39.6."},"rear-figure-scale":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - HIG page 12, the Figure 8 fan-overview elevation, which draws the whole rear face. Faceplate 3897 x 381 px (x 758-4654, y 1117-1497): 8.857 px/mm on 440 and 8.759 px/mm on 43.5, 1.1% apart, so the same gate passes. The rear is NOT mirrored here - the figure is drawn from behind the unit and the modules are horizontal, so left-to-right in the figure is left-to-right in the rear view."},"reset-button":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - a small ring at centre (136.0, 38.8), about 2.2 mm across, labelled RST to its right. Drawn with common/reset-button (4.0 x 4.0, its own contract size) centred on that point, so it renders larger than the figure's ring; the figure does not resolve a 2 mm feature well enough to argue with the component."},"right":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured within a figure whose scale is anchored on the 302 mm depth. HIG section 8 says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed' and 'the designated location ... is located on the side of the router', and Figure 22 draws BOTH, labelled Location-1 and Location-2. Measured on that figure (chassis bar 768 px for 302 mm), Location-1's two M4 holes are at 9.4 and 25.2 mm and Location-2's at 193.3 and 209.0, on a 15.7-15.8 mm hole pitch that matches the accessory lug (50 x 11.1 x 7.5 mm, #6 AWG, 2 x M4*L8.0 screws). AXIS: x = 0 is the FRONT on a right view (viewer3d.js convention), and the front is taken as the figure's left end. WHICH FLANK IS NOT STATED - the HIG says only 'the side'. Drawn on the right because the front faceplate prints its earth symbol at the right-hand end; recorded as a gap rather than asserted."},"rj45-block":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - ports 0-3 in one white housing x 206.7-239.7, y 8.9-35.7. The white bezel walls inside it read at x 208.6-210.6, 221.3-224.5 and 235.2-239.0, so the two jack columns are centred at 215.95 and 229.85: a 13.9 mm column pitch, which is exactly what std/rj45-ganged's 12.7 contract was measured for and well under the 16 mm std/rj45 bezel. Rows at y 10.0 and 23.9, separated by a white land at 20.7-23.9. NUMBERING RUNS DOWN COLUMNS - 0 over 1, 2 over 3 - which is the vendor's own print, small white numerals above and below the housing at the column centres. The top row is keyway-up (rotate 180) with its lamps in the top corners and the bottom row keyway-down with its lamps in the bottom corners; lamp positions colour-measured at x 211.0/220.9 and 224.9/234.8, y 10.9 (top) and 32.6 (bottom)."},"sfp-plus-row":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - ports 12-17 in TWO housings, not one: a two-column block x 364.9-395.5 and a single column x 397.6-413.3, with a 2 mm land between them that the vendor's own blue paint respects. Blue bands run above (y 6.6-8.9) and below (y 35.6-37.9) each housing and the port numerals are printed dark ON the blue, so the bands are faceplate paint and live in panel.decor - silkscreen paints over decor and under components, which is the only arrangement in which the numerals stay readable. Cage columns from the lamp pairs at 373.2, 387.9 and 405.5; drawn at 365.85, 380.1 and 398.3 on the standard 14.25 pitch inside each housing, which lands the first two 0.6 mm from their measured centres and the third on it."},"sfp-row":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - ports 4-11, four columns of two in one light housing x 303.7-362.4, y 8.9-35.6. Rows at y 9.1 and 25.1. g.data-description: HIG GNSS row - Off (GNSS not configured), Solid Green (normal state, self-survey complete), Blinking Green (learning state, self-survey not complete), Solid Yellow (power up, not tracking any satellite), Blinking Yellow (antenna short to ground). Every row but Solid Yellow is annotated "need NOS to activate this feature"
g.title: led-gnss

g.data-description: HIG SYNC row - Off (timing synchronization disabled or free-run), Solid Green (timing core, 1588 and SyncE, synchronized to an external source such as GNSS, 1PPS, PTP or BITS), Blinking Green (synchronized in SyncE mode), Solid Yellow (acquiring state or holdover), Blinking Yellow (synchronization fail)
g.title: led-sync

g.data-description: HIG STAT row - Off (X86 and BMC initializing, or not powered), Solid Green (system boot complete under the NOS), Blinking Green (system is booting), Solid Yellow (system boot complete under the DIAG OS). The yellow row is this family's difference from the S9510-28DC, whose table has none
g.title: led-stat

g.data-description: HIG FAN row - Off (X86 and BMC initializing, or not powered), Solid Green (all fan modules work well), Blinking Yellow (one or more fan modules fail or no fan module present)
g.title: led-fan

g.data-description: HIG PWR row - Off (no power or shutdown), Solid Green (system power good, BMC present and BMC power good), Blinking Green (system power good, BMC present but BMC power fail), Solid Yellow (system power good but BMC absent), Blinking Yellow (system power fail)
g.title: led-pwr

g.data-description: led-mgmt-l: HIG Management port LED table, Left LED - Off (1G no link), Solid Green (1G link-up), Blinking Green (1G TX/RX activity); led-mgmt-r: HIG Management port LED table, Right LED - Off (no activity), Solid Amber (10M/100M link-up), Blinking Amber (10M/100M TX/RX activity). The two lamps do not share a vocabulary, which is why each is declared on its own
g.title: mgmt
